summary: When location tracking stops, Nora now says where the record ends instead of reporting the last place she saw someone as where they stayed.
details: Asked where someone is, an answer older than 45 minutes is now given as the last recorded position with its time, and Nora is told nothing was recorded after it, including when her live refresh got no answer. Before this, a position two hours old read as current.

Asked where someone has been, each person now carries the last time tracking recorded them, and anyone whose recording stops before the window ends is named. An empty stretch after that point is missing data, not the person staying put. Before this, a collector that stopped at midnight made a ride at 1am read as being home all night.
45 minutes is one missed Life360 heartbeat: over 14 days, a stationary phone still reported at least every 30 minutes, and every longer gap was shared by everyone at once.

Two new alerts: PresenceCollectionStalled when a circle has had no successful read for 30 minutes, and PresenceAuthRefused when Life360 refuses the collector's login or reads. The collector stopped for hours with a healthy container and nothing alerted.
limitations: This makes a stopped record visible; it does not restart one. A refused Life360 login still needs the operator to fix the credentials.
